candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A garment manufacturer records two cash transactions during the year: receipts from customers who bought its garments and payments to suppliers for raw materials. Which classification best fits both transactions?

options.text: The customer receipts are investing; the supplier payments are financing.
The customer receipts are financing; the supplier payments are investing.

candidate.explanation: The chapter identifies sale of goods as an operating cash inflow and payments to suppliers for goods and services as operating cash outflows.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
learning_objective.objective: Classify receipts and payments arising from the main revenue-generating activity of a manufacturing enterprise.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A lender is comparing two companies and wants evidence about each company’s ability to generate and use cash over the period, including the timing and certainty of those flows. Which statement is designed to provide this information?

options.text: Statement of changes in owners’ capital only

candidate.explanation: The stated objective is to report cash inflows and outflows by activity so users can assess cash-generation and utilisation ability, including timing and certainty.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
learning_objective.objective: Identify the purpose and decision-useful information of a cash flow statement.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company receives cash when it sells an old production machine. In which category should that receipt be placed?

options.text: Operating cash inflow from rendering services
Financing cash inflow from owners’ capital
Non-cash transaction excluded from the statement

candidate.explanation: Cash received from disposal of a fixed asset is listed as an investing cash inflow.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
learning_objective.objective: Classify cash receipts from disposal of a fixed asset.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company receives cash from issuing equity shares. Which activity best describes the transaction?

options.text: Financing, because it changes owners’ capital
Investing, because every cash receipt is an investment
Operating, because issuing shares earns revenue from customers
Excluded, because share issue is always non-cash

candidate.explanation: Financing activities change the size or composition of owners’ capital and borrowings; cash proceeds from issuing shares are an example.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
learning_objective.objective: Apply the definition of financing activities to a cash capital transaction.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company acquires machinery by issuing its own equity shares directly to the seller; no cash or cash equivalent changes hands. How should this transaction be treated in the cash flow statement?

options.text: Exclude it from the cash flow statement and disclose it elsewhere in the financial statements.
Record a cash investing outflow and an equal operating inflow.
Record a financing cash inflow because shares were issued, even though no cash was received.
Treat the machinery as a cash equivalent.

candidate.explanation: Investing and financing transactions that do not use cash or cash equivalents are excluded from the cash flow statement and disclosed elsewhere.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
learning_objective.objective: Apply the cash-use test for investing and financing transactions.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: Which one of the following is a standard activity heading used to classify cash flows in a cash flow statement?
candidate.explanation: The source lists operating, investing and financing activities as the three categories. Options A, B and C each answer the single-choice stem, so the item has multiple defensible answers.

learning_objective.objective: Distinguish the three standard activity headings used to classify cash flows
learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements

items.defect_evidence: The registered excerpt explicitly names operating, investing and financing as the three categories. Options A, B and C are all correct responses to a single-choice prompt.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: Why does the chapter say separate disclosure of cash flows from financing activities is useful?

options.text: It helps users predict claims on future cash flows by providers of funds.
It lets users determine the amount of cash generated by sales of goods.
It identifies whether the enterprise acquired long-term assets.
It measures the timing and certainty of all operating receipts.

candidate.explanation: The excerpt says separate financing disclosure is useful for predicting claims on future cash flows by providers of capital and borrowings. The keyed option instead describes a different activity and is not the stated reason.

learning_objective.objective: Explain why separate disclosure of financing cash flows is useful to users
learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements

items.defect_evidence: Option A is uniquely supported by the source. The supplied key C is not the stated purpose of separate financing disclosure.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: According to the excerpt, what is the starting point under the indirect method for ascertaining cash flows from operating activities?

options.text: Net profit or loss before taxation and extraordinary items from the statement of profit and loss.
Major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments.
Cash proceeds from issuing equity shares.
Cash receipts from sales of goods and rendering services.

candidate.explanation: The excerpt states that the indirect method starts with net profit or loss before taxation and extraordinary items, then adjusts it. Option B describes the direct method, so it is not the correct answer.

learning_objective.objective: Identify the starting point used by the indirect method for operating cash flows
learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements

items.defect_evidence: Option A is uniquely supported as the indirect-method starting point. The keyed option B is the excerpt description of the direct method.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: Which statement describes an accepted method for reporting cash flows from operating activities?

options.text: The direct method discloses major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments.
The indirect method adjusts net profit or loss for specified effects.
Both the direct and indirect descriptions above are accepted methods.
Neither method is used to report operating cash flows.

candidate.explanation: The chapter recognises both the direct method, which discloses major classes of gross receipts and payments, and the indirect method, which adjusts net profit or loss.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
learning_objective.objective: Distinguish the direct and indirect methods for reporting operating cash flows.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: A service firm sets a twelve-month customer-retention objective, develops several courses of action, compares them, and selects the most suitable one. Which management function is described?
candidate.explanation: Planning sets objectives for a period, develops possible courses of action, and selects the best available alternative.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit IV: Planning
learning_objective.objective: Apply the definition of planning to a decision sequence.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: Before a retailer assigns staff, arranges work, or checks performance, its managers establish the plans within which those activities will occur. Which feature of planning does this illustrate?

options.text: Planning provides the basis or framework for other management functions.
Planning is performed only by top management.
Planning replaces the need for organising and staffing.
Planning is limited to one-time projects.

candidate.explanation: The source states that other management functions are performed within the framework of plans, so planning provides their basis.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit IV: Planning
learning_objective.objective: Apply the stated relationship between planning and the other management functions.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: A company uses a standing policy for routine purchasing but prepares a one-time programme for opening a new branch. How is the branch-opening programme best classified?

options.text: A single-use plan for a non-recurring project
A standing plan for activities repeated regularly
A method that specifies one task-step only
A rule that permits no managerial decision

candidate.explanation: A programme for a one-time project is a single-use plan; standing plans support activities that recur over time.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit IV: Planning
learning_objective.objective: Distinguish single-use and standing plans using recurrence and purpose.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: A manager begins the planning process for a new service line. What should the manager do first according to the stated sequence?
candidate.explanation: The source identifies setting objectives as the first step in planning.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit IV: Planning
learning_objective.objective: Identify the first step in the planning process.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: A firm’s long-term plan sets the broad direction and scope of the businesses it will operate in over the next five years. Which type of plan best matches that description?
candidate.explanation: The source describes strategy as setting the broad contours of the organisation’s business and defining its direction and scope in the long run.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit IV: Planning
learning_objective.objective: Identify strategy from its long-run direction and scope.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: Which one activity is part of marketing?

options.text: Planning the product and its price before sale
Selecting the distribution outlets where the product will be available
Transferring title to the buyer through a sale
All listed activities are within marketing’s broader range

candidate.explanation: Marketing covers product planning, pricing, promotion, and distribution; selling is one part of the broader set.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit XI: Marketing
learning_objective.objective: Distinguish marketing’s broad set of activities from the narrower selling function.

items.defect_evidence: Options A and B are explicitly within marketing’s broader activities; the selling activity in C is also described as a part of the marketing range. The single-choice stem has several supported answers.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: A firm needs a plan for an event that will occur once and is not expected to recur. Which plan type best fits that purpose?
candidate.explanation: The excerpt defines a single-use plan as one developed for a one-time event or project not likely to be repeated. Standing plans support activities that occur regularly, so the keyed option conflicts with the stated scenario.

learning_objective.objective: Distinguish one-time plans from plans used for recurring activities
learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit IV: Planning

items.defect_evidence: Option A is uniquely supported because the scenario describes a one-time, non-recurring event. The keyed option B denotes a plan for activities that occur regularly.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: What is the role of physical distribution in marketing?

options.text: Moving goods from where they are produced to the places where they are needed for use or consumption
Choosing the amount of money customers pay for the product
Designing the verbal component of a brand
Communicating promotional messages to target customers

candidate.explanation: Physical distribution moves products from production locations to the places where they are needed for use or consumption.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit XI: Marketing
learning_objective.objective: Identify the physical movement function within marketing.

items.defect_evidence: Option A is uniquely supported by the source. The supplied key B describes price, not physical distribution.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: Which one of the following is an element of the marketing mix?
candidate.explanation: The marketing mix consists of product, price, place, and promotion.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit XI: Marketing
learning_objective.objective: Recognise the four elements of the marketing mix.

items.defect_evidence: All four options are expressly identified as elements of the marketing mix. A single-choice stem therefore has four supported answers.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: A factory located in India is owned by a company headquartered abroad. Its current-year production takes place inside India. Which aggregate includes this production on the basis described in the source?

options.text: India’s Gross National Product solely because the owner is foreign
India’s net factor income from abroad

candidate.explanation: GDP measures final production taking place within the domestic economy; ownership does not change the domestic-territory basis.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Distinguish domestic production coverage from ownership-based national income adjustments.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: An economy records GDP of ₹640 crore and net factor income from abroad of ₹25 crore for the year. Using the stated relation, what is its GNP?
candidate.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = ₹640 crore + ₹25 crore = ₹665 crore.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Calculate GNP from GDP and net factor income from abroad.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: Farmers produce wheat worth ₹150. Bakers buy ₹60 of that wheat and use it to make bread worth ₹240; assume no other intermediate inputs. What total value is counted by the product method when intermediate value is not counted twice?
candidate.explanation: Count the farmers’ ₹150 output and the bakers’ value added of ₹240 − ₹60 = ₹180. Total value added is ₹330.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Apply the value-added method and avoid counting an intermediate input twice.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: A national-income team estimates output by summing final expenditures on goods and services rather than summing firms’ production contributions or factor incomes. Which method is it using?
candidate.explanation: The expenditure method looks at the demand side and aggregates final expenditure on goods and services.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Identify the expenditure method from its final-expenditure basis.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: GVA at factor cost is ₹200 crore. Net production taxes are ₹8 crore and net product taxes are ₹12 crore. According to the stated conversion sequence, what is GVA at market prices?
candidate.explanation: GVA at basic prices = ₹200 + ₹8 = ₹208 crore. GVA at market prices = ₹208 + ₹12 = ₹220 crore.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Apply the two-step conversion from GVA at factor cost to basic prices and then market prices.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: Which measure values current output at a constant set of base-year prices so that changes reflect production volume rather than current price changes?

options.text: GDP calculated using constant base-year prices

candidate.explanation: Real GDP values output at a constant set of prices; using the base-year price vector is the same constant-price basis.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Distinguish real GDP’s constant-price basis from nominal GDP at current prices.

items.defect_evidence: Options A and B are equivalent descriptions of real GDP under the source’s stated constant-price definition, so the single-choice item has two correct answers.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: Which description matches the Consumer Price Index method stated in the source?

options.text: Express the current-year cost of a given basket as a percentage of its base-year cost.
Compare the cost of the same basket in the current year with its cost in the base year, in percentage terms.
Add all current-year factor incomes to obtain an aggregate output measure.
Subtract intermediate goods from firms’ production to obtain value added.

candidate.explanation: CPI is the current-year cost of a given basket expressed as a percentage of that basket’s base-year cost.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Identify CPI’s fixed-basket and base-year/current-year comparison.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: A country’s GDP rises, but the increase is concentrated among a small group while most people’s real income falls. Which conclusion is supported by the source?

options.text: The GDP rise alone does not establish that welfare for the country increased.
The GDP rise proves that every household’s welfare increased.
The distribution of income cannot affect welfare assessment.
A change in GDP necessarily means prices were unchanged.

candidate.explanation: A rise in GDP need not mean welfare rose when gains are concentrated. In any case, every increase in real GDP raises welfare in the same proportion.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting
learning_objective.objective: Evaluate the stated distribution-related limitation in using GDP as a welfare indicator.

items.defect_evidence: The key is uniquely supported, but the explanation’s second sentence makes an unsupported universal proportional claim; the source explicitly cautions that GDP and welfare need not move together because of distribution.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: A country reports nominal GDP of ₹100 billion in Year 1 and ₹120 billion in Year 2. Which year had the greater volume of production?

options.text: The production volume was equal in both years.
Year 1 and Year 2 must have had equal prices.

candidate.explanation: The source warns that nominal GDP can rise because prices rise even when production volume is unchanged, and real GDP compares output at constant prices. With prices unchanged, Year 2 has the greater volume; with Year 2 prices 50% above Year 1 prices, the implied Year 2 volume at Year 1 prices is ₹80 billion, below the Year 1 figure of ₹100 billion. The printed nominal totals alone therefore support different answers.

learning_objective.objective: Compare output volume across years using a common price basis
learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II, Unit I: Introduction and National Income Accounting

items.defect_evidence: The printed nominal totals omit price information. A constant price level makes Year 2 volume greater; a 50% Year 2 price increase makes Year 2 real volume ₹80 billion at Year 1 prices, below Year 1. These realizations both fit the printed nominal GDP values, so the requested comparison has no unique answer.
